title: AWS EC2 instance is unreachable
content: Check that the instance is running and passes status checks. Verify the security group allows the required inbound port, the subnet route table and internet gateway or VPN path are correct, network ACLs permit traffic, and the operating system firewall is not blocking access. For SSH, check the username, key pair, and port 22; for RDP, check port 3389.

title: AWS S3 Access Denied or 403 error
content: Check the IAM identity policy, bucket policy, and any organization service control policies. Confirm the resource ARN and requested action are correct. Check whether S3 Block Public Access, an explicit deny, an encryption key policy, or a VPC endpoint policy blocks the request. Avoid making buckets public as a troubleshooting shortcut.

title: CloudWatch logs are missing
content: Confirm the application or service is configured to send logs to the expected log group and stream. Check the time range, region, log group name, IAM permissions, agent status, and delivery configuration. Verify that the workload role has the required CloudWatch Logs permissions.

title: Azure virtual machine Remote Desktop connection fails
content: Confirm the VM is running and review Boot diagnostics. Check Network Security Group rules, routing, the VM guest firewall, the Remote Desktop service, and whether the correct username and destination are used. Use Azure Bastion or the documented repair and troubleshooting options when available.

title: Azure Blob Storage authorization failure
content: Check the storage account and container name, the signed-in identity, and the required Azure RBAC data role. Confirm the token has not expired and that network rules, firewall settings, and shared access signature permissions and expiry are correct. Allow time for role assignment changes to propagate.

title: Azure Monitor Logs query returns no results
content: Check the selected workspace, time range, table name, and query filters. Confirm diagnostic settings or agents are configured to send data to the workspace. Newly ingested data may take time to appear. Test with a broad query before adding restrictive filters.

title: Google Cloud VM SSH connection fails
content: Confirm the VM is running and check network tags, firewall rules, routes, and the destination port. Verify OS Login or SSH key configuration and IAM permissions. Review serial console output and guest-agent status where available. Do not open SSH to all internet addresses unless required and secured.

title: Google Cloud Storage permission denied
content: Verify the active principal, project, bucket, and required IAM permissions. Check bucket-level and project-level IAM policies, uniform bucket-level access settings, and any organization policies. Ensure the application is using the intended service account credentials.

title: Google Cloud logs are missing
content: Check the project and resource filter, time range, log name, and severity filters. Verify that the workload has permission to write logs and that the relevant logging agent or integration is configured. Start with a broad query to confirm whether any entries are arriving.

title: Kubernetes pod is crashing or stuck in CrashLoopBackOff
content: Run kubectl describe pod POD_NAME and inspect Events. Check current and previous container logs with kubectl logs POD_NAME and kubectl logs POD_NAME --previous. Review the application command, environment variables, mounted configuration, secrets references, probes, resource limits, image availability, and dependencies. Compare with the last working deployment.

title: Kubernetes Service cannot reach the application
content: Check that the Service selector matches pod labels and that endpoints exist. Confirm containerPort, targetPort, service port, and readiness probes. Use kubectl get svc,endpoints,pods and inspect network policies, DNS, and ingress configuration as applicable.

title: Kubernetes Deployment is not updating
content: Check rollout status with kubectl rollout status deployment/NAME and inspect kubectl describe deployment NAME. Verify the image tag, image pull permissions, pod events, readiness probes, quotas, and rollout strategy. Review ReplicaSets and consider a rollback if a release is causing an outage.

title: Docker container exits immediately
content: Inspect the exit code and run docker logs CONTAINER_NAME. Check the container command and entrypoint, required environment variables, mounted files, application startup errors, and whether the main process stays in the foreground. Reproduce the image locally with the same configuration while avoiding printing secrets.

title: Docker image build fails
content: Read the first meaningful error in the build output. Check Dockerfile syntax, build context, file paths, .dockerignore, package repositories, dependency versions, and network access. Build one stage at a time when using multi-stage builds and avoid copying secret files into images.

title: Linux service fails to start
content: Use systemctl status SERVICE and journalctl -u SERVICE to inspect the failure. Check configuration syntax, file permissions, required environment variables, dependencies, disk space, and port conflicts. Validate configuration before restarting a production service.

title: Git push is rejected
content: Read the rejection message. If the remote contains commits not present locally, fetch and integrate those changes before pushing. Confirm the current branch and remote, resolve conflicts carefully, and avoid force-pushing shared branches unless the team explicitly agrees.

title: CI/CD pipeline fails during build or deployment
content: Identify the first failing step and inspect its full logs. Check runner environment, dependency versions, secrets configuration, permissions, artifact paths, test failures, and environment-specific settings. Reproduce the command locally when possible and do not print secret values in logs.

title: Python application raises an exception
content: Read the full traceback from the bottom upward to identify the exception type and the line where it originated. Check variable values and types, input assumptions, file paths, and the calling function. Create a minimal reproducible example and add targeted logging without exposing secrets.

title: Python ModuleNotFoundError or ImportError
content: Confirm the intended virtual environment is activated and that python and pip refer to the same environment. Check the package name, install the required dependency into that environment, and verify the import name. Look for local files shadowing standard-library or package names, and check dependency declarations.

title: Python application cannot read environment variables
content: Check that the environment variable is defined in the process environment and that the application loads the intended .env file if using a dotenv library. Verify the working directory and file path. Never commit .env files or print API keys; restart the application after changing environment settings.

title: Java application fails with ClassNotFoundException
content: Check the full class name, package declaration, build output, and runtime classpath. Confirm required dependencies are included in the launched application and that the build and runtime use compatible versions. Rebuild cleanly and inspect the launch command or deployment packaging.

title: JavaScript application throws a runtime error
content: Read the browser console or Node.js stack trace and identify the first application frame. Check undefined or null values, asynchronous errors, input types, and the source map. Reduce the issue to a small reproducible example and add validation around external data.

title: SQL query returns unexpected results
content: Check join conditions, filters, NULL handling, grouping, aggregation, and date boundaries. Test each condition separately and inspect a small sample of source rows. Confirm whether duplicate rows or implicit type conversions affect the result before changing production data.

title: MySQL database connection fails
content: Verify hostname, port, database name, credentials, network reachability, and server status. Check bind-address, firewall rules, connection limits, TLS requirements, and the account's host permissions. Avoid putting passwords in source code or shared logs.

title: REST API returns HTTP 401 or 403
content: A 401 commonly indicates missing or invalid authentication; a 403 commonly indicates the identity lacks permission. Check the authorization header format, token expiry, scopes or roles, target environment, and API policy. Do not paste access tokens into logs or chat.

title: REST API returns HTTP 429 Too Many Requests
content: Check provider rate limits and response headers, then reduce request frequency. Add exponential backoff with jitter, respect Retry-After when supplied, and cache repeated reads where appropriate. Confirm quota and billing status in the provider dashboard without exposing credentials.

title: LLM API request fails due to quota or rate limits
content: Check the provider dashboard for billing, quota, and rate-limit status. Distinguish quota exhaustion from a temporary rate limit, reduce concurrency, implement bounded retries with backoff for transient errors, and handle failures gracefully. Never expose API keys in code, screenshots, or logs.

title: RAG application retrieves irrelevant documents
content: Inspect the exact query and the top retrieved results. Check document quality, chunk size, metadata, embedding model consistency, similarity metric, and relevance threshold. Evaluate retrieval on representative questions and unrelated questions, and tune ranking using measured results rather than assuming a score is confidence.

title: Embedding similarity search gives poor matches
content: Ensure query and document embeddings are generated with the same compatible model and preprocessing. Check vector dimensions, normalization, similarity metric, text quality, and language. Compare known related and unrelated pairs and inspect the retrieved documents, not only a single score.

title: LLM answer contains unsupported information
content: Provide the model with relevant retrieved evidence, clearly instruct it to distinguish evidence from assumptions, and allow it to say when information is insufficient. Display sources, evaluate answers against test questions, and avoid treating generated text as verified facts. Do not claim the model inspected systems it cannot access.

title: Website or REST API returns HTTP 503 Service Unavailable
content: HTTP 503 Service Unavailable means the server is temporarily unable to handle the request, commonly because of overload, maintenance, or an unavailable upstream dependency. Check whether the issue affects all routes or only one endpoint. Inspect server, load balancer, reverse proxy, and application logs around the failure time. Check health checks, upstream service availability, connection pools, resource saturation, and recent deployments. Retry only when appropriate, using bounded exponential backoff with jitter; respect Retry-After if provided. Do not confuse HTTP 503 with HTTP 429 Too Many Requests, which indicates rate limiting. If using a managed platform, check its service health and status page.
